news.title: Huge audience numbers achieved by TVNZ coverage of FIFA Men’s World Cup
news.lede: National broadcaster TVNZ has secured exclusive rights to the 2030 FIFA Men’s World Cup after drawing huge audiences during this year’s tournament. TVNZ has the rights for free-to-air and pay-to-watch games at the 2030 tournament to be co-hosted by Spain, Portugal and Morocco. Chief executive Jodi O’Donnell said the World Cup was a “standout moment for football in Aotearoa and for TVNZ”. The tournament was the biggest event in TVNZ+ history, with more than 20 million streams recorded for the 104 matches.

news.title: Pirlo out of Italy football top job after backlash over Russian betting firm links
news.lede: Andrea Pirlo has said he is no longer a candidate to coach the Italian national side following days of controversy over his ties to a Russian betting company. His appointment as Italy's next head coach had not been confirmed by the Italian Football Federation (FIGC) yet was being treated as all but certain. But over the weekend several Italian politicians criticised the FIGC's choice, noting that Pirlo, 47, had taken up a role as global ambassador for Russia's Fonbet last October. Hours later, Italian football was plunged further into crisis as it was reported by Sky Sport Italia that two other senior figures in the FIGC, Paolo Maldini and Leonardo, had decided to resign.

news.title: Mexico national football team: full squad and key players
news.lede: Mexico won all three group games at their home World Cup and ended a 40-year knockout drought before England stopped them. Here is the full 26-man squad, the players who mattered, and what changes under Rafael Marquez. Mexico went into a home World Cup in 2026 carrying four decades of the same question, and for about a week it looked like they had finally answered it. They won all three group games without conceding, beat Ecuador at the Azteca for their first knockout win since 1986, and then lost to England on the same ground.

news.title: 'Sorry you were so consumed by hate' - Gianni Infantino blasts FIFA critics after 'most outstanding' World Cup
news.lede: FIFA president Gianni Infantino has hit back at his detractors in extraordinary fashion, claiming that those who criticised the 2026 World Cup were "consumed by hate." In a lengthy and defiant statement, the head of world football’s governing body defended the tournament’s legacy and urged his opponents to "meditate or pray" instead of spreading negativity. In the wake of a tournament that was as much defined by its off-field drama as its on-field heroics, Infantino has chosen to go on the offensive. The FIFA president used his personal Instagram and the organisation’s official channels to deliver a stinging rebuke to the journalists and critics who questioned the logistics and integrity of the 2026 World Cup across the United States, Canada, and Mexico.

news.title: Chelsea launch surprise move to sign England World Cup star on free transfer
news.lede: Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso (Picture: EPA) Chelsea are working on a surprise move to sign Brentford and England midfielder Jordan Henderson on a free transfer, according to reports. Multiple Premier League clubs are said to be interested in completing a deal for Henderson, who made 32 league appearances for Brentford last season. But widespread reports indicate that Chelsea are leading the way to sign the 36-year-old as they look to add much-needed experience to Xabi Alonso’s squad. Henderson, who captained Liverpool to Premier League glory in 2020, is said to be open to the move across London.

news.title: Infantino slams World Cup critics for ‘spreading hate’
news.lede: PARIS: FIFA president Gianni Infantino has hit back at World Cup critics, claiming they were "spreading hate and false rumours” and arguing the tournament delivered "only joy and happiness”. In a long open letter published on Monday, Infantino urged detractors to "take a moment to reflect, meditate, pray” after a tournament marked by controversies ranging from ticket pricing to visa issues. "Sorry that you were so consumed by hate and criticism that you missed it all,” Infantino wrote in a post shared on his Instagram account and FIFA’s official channels. "To those behind their pens and papers, behind their screens, spreading hate and false rumours, I want to say that while you are sitting behind, we at FIFA are on the front lines organising, working hard, and delivering the best show in the world.

news.title: Lopes Cabral's curling goal against Argentina voted FIFA World Cup's best goal
news.lede: Cape Verde added another chapter to its World Cup journey on Monday after Sidny Lopes Cabral won the public vote for the Goal of the Tournament.Lopes Cabral earned the honour for his curling strike into the top corner against Argentina during the 2026 FIFA World Cup. The goal came in extra time of Cape Verde's Round of 32 match in Miami Gardens, drawing his side level at 2-2 against the defending champions. Argentina, however, went on to win the match 3-2. The 2026 edition marked Cape Verde's first appearance at the FIFA World Cup.

news.title: Infantino blasts World Cup critics for 'spreading hate' in long rant
news.lede: This content is provided by Exco Player and may use cookies or similar technologies. Please click 'Allow and Continue' below to load the content. Gianni Infantino has launched an extraordinary defence of FIFA’s handling of the World Cup, accusing critics of “spreading hate and false rumours” and telling them to “reflect, meditate and pray”. The expanded 48-team men’s 2026 tournament - co-hosted by the United States, Canada and Mexico - finished last weekend when Spain beat Argentina 1-0 in the final after extra time.
